violation_type.title: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 12 or Fewer Children (26 TAC §746.1701)
violation_type.typical_finding: One caregiver was observed in direct care of 11 children with three of those children being ages 0-17 months of age; the maximum number of children to be   supervised by one caregiver was 7, therefore the caregiver was over by 4 children.

finding_variants.text: One caregiver was observed in direct care of 11 children with three of those children being ages 0-17 months of age; the maximum number of children to be   supervised by one caregiver was 7, therefore the caregiver was over by 4 children.
A caregiver was observed careing for the following ages alone: 12m, 18m, 3yr, 2yr, 3yr, 3yr, 2yr and 3yr.

During inspection, there were seven children in care with one caregiver. There were two infants under eighteen months combined with five children between the ages of eighteen months and four years. According to minimum standards, there can only be four children or less age eighteen months to four years combined with two infants under eighteen months if there is only one caregiver present.     This was corrected at inspection when another caregiver arrived and the operation was brought into ratio compliance.
There were 6 infants under the care of 1 caregiver. The specified age of the group was 12-17 months old.       NOTE: A second caregiver entered the classroom and child-caregiver ratio was met.
During the monitoring visit, one caregiver had ten children. Four children were aged 0-17 months, and six were aged 18 months-4 years.

During inspection one caregiver was present with 11 children ages 12m-4years. One additional caregiver was needed to meet ratio. This was corrected at inspection when a staff member arrived for their shift.

occurrences.finding: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 12 or Fewer Children: The center was out of compliance with ratios for when 12 or fewer children are in care on the following days: 12/3/25, 12/4/25, 12/5/25, 12/11/25, 12/19/25, 12/23/25, 1/7/26, 1/8/26, 1/9/26 and 1/12/26. Child/Caregiver Ratio - 12 or Fewer Children: CCR observed the operation operating out of ratio for a total of less than 12 children present.  There are 9 children present. 1 child ranging from 0 to 17 months, 7 children ranging from 18 months to 4 years, and one child ranging from 5 years..  The ratio should be 1 child ranging from 0 to 17 months, 5 children ranging from 18 month to 4 years, and 1 child ranging from 5 years and older. One caregiver can supervise 5 children  ranging from 18 months to 4 years present. The operation is over ratio by 2 children ranging from 18 months to 4 years.   The deficiency was corrected during the inspection when 2 children ranging from 18 months to 4 years were picked up by parents.
